observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000022`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

22. **FOS-000022 — Describe reuse evidence and compatibility honestly.** **M; depends on `FOS-000006`, `FOS-000011`, `FOS-000012`, `FOS-000013`, `FOS-000014`, `FOS-000021`; §5–§6.** Report separate facts for replayer-cache marker skips ([replay:3144](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L3144)), application pipeline-cache feedback ([replay:1479](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1479)), shader identifiers and opaque driver-managed caches. Include build/tool version, input identities, effective filters/options, null-device mode, device/driver/API and relevant UUID context, deadlines and duration units. Existing GPU and timing logs are useful but not a retained structured context record. **Check:** unavailable feedback stays unknown, simulated null-device run cannot claim GPU warming, legacy markers do not prove persistence, changed device/driver context is visible. Metadata alone is not proof of cache hits. Steam's scheduling rationale remains outside Fossilize's evidence.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Context and evidence-classification tests:** Marker skip, reported application-cache hit/miss, shader identifier and unavailable driver-cache feedback remain separate fields/facts. Null-device success cannot claim GPU warming; legacy markers, replay success and checked close cannot claim verified reuse or power-loss durability.
   - **Deterministic context fixtures and hardware integration:** Reports preserve known version/input/filter/device/driver/API/UUID/deadline context with explicit unknowns and fixed duration units; changing context changes the relevant identity fields. A registered hardware job asserts feedback facts on a capable device. Missing hardware is reported skipped/unverified, never as a passing cache-reuse test.
